title: Credit-card default
problem: A lender wants to flag accounts likely to miss next month's payment. Inputs are billing history, payment amounts, and demographics. False alarms create extra manual review, and missed defaults are costly.

title: Hospital readmission
problem: Predict 30-day unplanned readmission from labs, diagnoses, and length of stay. Many fields are missing, and the labeled set is modest. Clinicians want a probability they can review.

title: Subscription churn
problem: Score whether a subscriber will cancel this week so a retention offer can be shown in the app. The feature vector is usage counts and plan type. Scoring must stay on a small CPU service.

title: Card fraud
problem: Classify a transaction as fraudulent from amount, merchant category, and velocity features. Fraud is rare. Investigators can only review a small queue, so precision at the top of the list matters.

title: Species presence
problem: Classify whether a rare plant is present in a plot using soil, rainfall, and elevation measurements. Only a few hundred labeled plots exist, and several predictors are correlated.

title: Line defect
problem: Detect defective parts from sensor summaries on a manufacturing line. The process drifts after tool changes, so a model fit once on last year's data is not enough.

title: Student dropout
problem: Flag students who may leave before the next term using grades, attendance, and enrollment features. The school requires error rates to be checked across demographic groups before any outreach list is used.

title: Lab risk flag
problem: From routine blood-test panels, flag patients for a follow-up test. Missing a true positive is worse than an extra test, and probabilities should be reasonably calibrated.

title: Campaign response
problem: Predict who will respond to a promotion. Features mix numeric spend history with high-cardinality categorical fields. Analysts want per-prediction explanations they can show to marketing.

title: Noisy sensor failure
problem: Classify whether a pump is about to fail from noisy tabular sensor aggregates. Labels exist for only a fraction of windows, and several channels drop out at random.

title: Personal loan default
problem: Predict default on a personal loan from application form fields and a short repayment history. A regulator may ask why an application was scored as high risk.

title: ICU mortality risk
problem: Estimate in-hospital mortality risk from the first six hours of ICU vitals and labs stored as a flat table. Missingness is informative. The output is a risk band for a review huddle, not an automated order.

title: Spam filter features
problem: Classify email as spam from a fixed tabular vector of token counts and header flags. The mailbox stream is large and the decision has to be made when the message arrives.

title: Crop disease
problem: Classify a field plot as diseased or healthy from weather, soil, and scouting counts. The growing season yields few labeled plots, and two soil measures move together.

title: Employee attrition
problem: Predict whether an employee will leave within six months from HRIS fields such as tenure, role, and overtime. HR will not use a score that cannot be explained to a manager.

title: Intrusion records
problem: Label a network flow record as attack or benign using duration, bytes, and protocol flags. Attacks are rare and the sensor exports tens of thousands of rows per minute.

title: Product return
problem: Predict whether an online order will be returned using basket size, category, discount, and customer history. The loss from a return is modest, so a simple model is preferred unless a complex one clearly helps.

title: Diabetes screening table
problem: Using age, BMI, blood pressure, and a few lab fields, flag patients for a diabetes follow-up. The clinic wants high recall and a score that is not wildly miscalibrated.

title: Parcel fire risk
problem: Classify land parcels as high or low wildfire risk next month from weather summaries, vegetation indexes, and distance to roads. The table is wide and some satellite fields are missing on cloudy days.

title: Water quality exceedance
problem: Predict whether a sensor site will exceed a contaminant threshold tomorrow from recent readings and upstream flow. Labels are sparse because lab confirmation is slow.

title: Insurance claim complexity
problem: Route an insurance claim to a senior adjuster when it is likely to be complex. Inputs are claim type, amounts, and a few categorical codes. Most claims are routine.

title: Battery pack fault
problem: Classify a battery pack as faulty from tabular summaries of voltage, temperature, and cycle count. Failures are rare and a false alarm pulls a pack off the line.

title: Scholarship completion
problem: Predict which scholarship recipients are at risk of not completing the term, using credits, GPA, and hours worked. Any outreach list must be checked for large error gaps across groups.

title: Phishing URL table
problem: Classify a URL as phishing from a hand-built table of length, token, and host features. Decisions happen in the browser extension, so the model has to stay small.

title: Machine maintenance
problem: Predict whether a machine needs maintenance this week from vibration and temperature aggregates. The plant can explain a tree or a linear model more easily than a deep model to technicians.

title: Microloan repayment
problem: Predict repayment difficulty for a microloan from business type, prior loans, and a few household fields. The sample is small and several categories have few examples.

title: Severe airline delay
problem: Classify whether a flight will be delayed by more than an hour using schedule, carrier, and weather-table features available at departure minus two hours.

title: Housing distress
problem: Flag properties at risk of housing distress from tax, permit, and neighborhood tabular fields. City staff need a short reason code with each flag.

title: Lab batch failure
problem: Predict whether a laboratory batch will fail quality control from instrument settings and reagent lots. Failed batches are uncommon and the scientific lead wants a model that is easy to retrain when a reagent changes.

title: Site occupancy from counts
problem: Classify a trail site as high animal activity tonight from a table of prior counts, weather, and moon phase. There is no image input. Labels cover two seasons only.
